notes: Added from help page "UPDATEFIELD (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a text with a Date field, run UPDATEFIELD, and assert it shows the current date.

statement: Dino 8 must compile SHP shape definition files (header '*number,defbytes,name' followed by comma-separated specification bytes ending in 0, 128-char lines, semicolon comments) into SHX files usable as shapes or, when the first entry describes the font, as fonts.
notes: Added from help page "About Shape Descriptions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: compile a SHP containing '*230,6,DBOX' with bytes '014,010,01C,018,012,0' and expect an SHX file with shape 230 loadable by LOAD.

statement: Dino 8 must decode three-character vector specification bytes (leading 0, hexadecimal length 1 to F, hexadecimal direction code of 16 directions, diagonals stretching to match the orthogonal vector) when drawing shapes and font glyphs.

source.ref: About Vector Length and Direction Codes

notes: Added from help page "About Vector Length and Direction Codes"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: compile DBOX with '014,010,01C,018,012,0', insert it with SHAPE at height 1 and expect a unit box with one diagonal.

statement: Dino 8 must implement the special shape specification codes 0 through 14 (end, pen down/up, divide/multiply scale, push/pop with a four-deep stack, subshape, X-Y displacement, polyline displacements, arcs, and so on) including the position stack overflow and underflow messages.
notes: Added from help page "Special Codes Reference"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: draw a shape that pushes five locations without pops and expect the message 'Position stack overflow in shape nnn'; use '8,(-10,3)' and expect a vector 10 left and 3 up.

statement: Dino 8 must read SHP text fonts where shape numbers equal character codes, with required shape 0 giving font name, above, below and modes (0 horizontal, 2 dual-orientation) and a line-feed shape 10 controlling line spacing.
notes: Added from help page "About Text Font Descriptions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: compile a font whose shape 0 is '*0,4,TESTFONT 21,7,2,0' and expect STYLE to accept it; edit the LF shape drop distance and expect multi-line text spacing to change.

statement: Dino 8 must support Unicode SHP fonts whose header is '*UNIFONT,6,name above,below,modes,encoding,type,0' with encoding and embedding-permission fields, and treat code 7 subshape references as two-byte values.
notes: Added from help page "About Unicode Font Descriptions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: compile a Unicode font containing '*00080,4,keuroRef 7,020AC,0' and expect the euro glyph to render via the subshape reference.

statement: Dino 8 must support Big Font files, a form of shape definition file that handles large two-byte character sets such as Japanese, including defining, extending and using them in text styles.
notes: Added from help page "About Big Font Descriptions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: create a text style using a big font file and expect two-byte characters in a TEXT object to render using it.

statement: Dino 8 must parse the leading '*BIGFONT nchars,nranges,b1,e1,...' line of a Big Font file, using the listed ranges as escape codes that mark the first byte of a two-byte character code.
notes: Added from help page "About Defining a Big Font"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: load a big font with '*BIGFONT 60,1,124,124' and expect the sequence '|' plus a letter to select the corresponding two-byte shape.

statement: Dino 8 must support extended Big Font files that build composite characters from reusable primitives through subshape code followed by 0 with primitive number, base point, width and height, scaled by the font's character height and width header.

source.ref: About Defining an Extended Big Font File

notes: Added from help page "About Defining an Extended Big Font File"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: define an extended big font whose composite shape reuses one primitive twice at different base points and expect both to render at the given scale.

statement: Dino 8 must let a text style bind a normal font and a Big Font (entered as 'normal,big' in -STYLE), with leading or trailing commas changing only one of them, and display both file names when listing styles.

source.ref: About Using Big Font Text in a Drawing

notes: Added from help page "About Using Big Font Text in a Drawing"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: run -STYLE with 'txt,greek' then ',big2' and expect the normal font to remain txt and the big font to become big2.

statement: Dino 8 must allow a Big Font to supply extra special symbols through a seldom-used escape character (such as a vertical bar), bypassing the 255-shape limit and %%nnn entry of extended standard fonts.

source.ref: About Using a Big Font to Extend a Font

notes: Added from help page "About Using a Big Font to Extend a Font"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: use a Big Font whose escape code is | and type '|a' in text to render the Greek alpha glyph.

statement: Dino 8 must honor font shape definitions that shift the imaginary pen up or down and scale the font (with matching reverse codes) so SHX text can display superscripts and subscripts.

source.ref: About Superscripts and Subscripts in SHX Files

notes: Added from help page "About Superscripts and Subscripts in SHX Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: use a font modified with superscript start/end shapes on keypad keys and expect the enclosed characters raised and scaled down, then back to normal.

statement: Dino 8 must compile SHP shape and font files into SHX with the COMPILE command, load shape files with LOAD, insert shapes with SHAPE at a chosen scale and rotation, and use compiled fonts through STYLE.

source.ref: About Compiling Shape and Font Files

notes: Added from help page "About Compiling Shape and Font Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Scenario: compile dbox.shp, run LOAD dbox.shx, run SHAPE DBOX at scale 2 and expect a 2-unit box inserted.

statement: Dino 8 must support annotation objects (dimensions, notes, symbols) that can be annotative or non-annotative, scaled according to the drawing or viewport scale.
notes: Added from help page "About Annotation Objects"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create an annotative text and a non-annotative text in a scaled viewport and assert the annotative one scales while the other keeps its fixed size.

statement: Dino 8 must calculate annotation scale for text height and annotation objects in model space and on layouts, using the drawing or plot scale or viewport scale, with annotative objects assigned scales.
notes: Added from help page "About Annotation Scale"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set viewport scale to 1:50 and assert annotative text height is multiplied accordingly; assign a second scale and assert both representations.

statement: Dino 8 must support the workflow for non-annotative annotation: set a style, create the object at a size computed for the final scale, then place it on layouts and viewports without automatic resizing.
notes: Added from help page "About Non-Annotative Objects Workflow"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create text at a computed height for 1:100 in model space, view it in a 1:100 viewport and assert plotted size is correct; change viewport scale and assert it does not change.

statement: Dino 8 must support the annotative workflow: set an annotative style, set the current annotation scale, create objects that resize automatically to the current scale, and show them per viewport scale.
notes: Added from help page "About Annotative Objects Workflow"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set annotation scale 1:50, create annotative text and assert it displays at the scaled height; change viewport scale and assert it resizes.

statement: Dino 8 must offer single-line text (independent objects) and multiline text supporting wrapping, character formatting, columns, stacked text, bullets and numbering, tabs and indents.
notes: Added from help page "About Creating Notes Using Text"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create multiline text with a bulleted list and two columns and assert the layout; create single-line text and assert it is a separate object.

statement: Dino 8 must support multiline text justification relative to the insertion point and boundary rectangle, columns with the in-place editor and column grips, and other paragraph formatting.
notes: Added from help page "About Multiline Text Format"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create mtext with middle-center justification and assert text flows around the insertion point; add columns and assert flow between columns.

statement: Dino 8 must provide named text styles (font, line spacing, justification, color and so on) selected as current for new text, with style changes updating all text using them and per-object overrides.
notes: Added from help page "About Text Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create style Notes with font Arial, create text, change the style font and assert the text updates; override one object and assert it keeps the override.

statement: Dino 8 must support fields in any text (except tolerances), including table cells and attributes, inserted from the shortcut menu, showing updatable data such as the file name and sheet set placeholders.
notes: Added from help page "About Using Fields in Text"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Insert a FileName field in text, rename the file, update fields and assert the text shows the new name.

statement: Dino 8 must support contextual fields (such as PlotOrientation, PaperSize, PlotScale, DeviceName, PageSetupName, CurrentSheetNumber) whose values depend on the layout or space they reside in, including inside blocks and xrefs.

source.ref: About Contextual Fields in Blocks and Xrefs

notes: Added from help page "About Contextual Fields in Blocks and Xrefs"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Place a PlotOrientation field on two layouts with different page setups and assert each displays its own value.

statement: A field can carry a hyperlink to a URL, file, saved view or layout that shows a hyperlink cursor and tooltip on hover and is followed with Ctrl+click, stays valid while the field is unchanged, and for sheet/view title and number fields keeps pointing at the right place when the sheet set changes.
notes: Added from help page "About Assigning Hyperlinks to Fields"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a Hyperlink field pointing at a saved view, hover to see the tooltip, Ctrl+click and assert the view is restored; rename the sheet in the sheet set and assert the sheet-title field link still jumps to that sheet.

statement: The program must let users rescale many text, mtext and attribute objects in place by relative factor, absolute height or match to existing text, and convert lengths between model and paper space units (SCALETEXT, SPACETRANS).
notes: Added from help page "About Changing Text Scale and Justification"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select 3 text objects of heights 2, 3 and 4, run SCALETEXT with factor 2 and assert heights become 4, 6 and 8 with insertion points unchanged.

statement: Find and Replace must search drawing text by content with wildcard patterns (digit, alpha, non-alphanumeric, any string, single char, negation, character sets and ranges) and replace only the characters while leaving formatting and properties untouched.
notes: Added from help page "About Finding and Replacing Text"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Replace 'ABC' with 'XYZ' in a bold red mtext containing 'ABC' and assert the text reads 'XYZ' with bold and red unchanged; search '?BC' and assert it matches 'ABC' and '3BC'.

statement: The program must spell-check single-line, multiline, dimension, multileader, attribute and xref text against selectable main and custom dictionaries (DCTMAIN, DCTCUST), highlighting and zooming to each misspelling and underlining misspelled words as the user types.
notes: Added from help page "About Spelling Check"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create text 'helo world', run Check Spelling and assert 'helo' is flagged with suggestions; add 'helo' to the custom dictionary and assert a rerun reports no errors.

statement: Multiline text entered via an alternate editor must support inline format codes for overline, underline, stacked fractions, alignment, height multipliers, and color/font changes, with grouping braces and paragraph breaks, rendering as the documented example does.

source.ref: Formatting multiline text in an alternate text editor

notes: Added from help page "About Formatting Multiline Text in an Alternate Text Editor"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Supply contents '{\H1.5x;Big}\P{\S1/2;}' and assert the mtext shows enlarged 'Big' on the first line and a stacked 1/2 fraction on the second.

statement: Dino 8's mtext parser and writer must recognize the full inline code table (\O \L \K toggles, \~ \\ \{ \} escapes, \C color, \F SHX and \f TrueType font, \H height, plus width, tracking, oblique, stack and alignment codes) and render them like AutoCAD.

source.ref: Format codes for alternate text editor

notes: Added from help page "Format Codes for Alternate Text Editor Reference"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Parse '\fCourier New;\C2;\LAB\l' and assert the run uses Courier New, color 2, with underline applied only to 'AB'.

statement: A table object must hold rows and columns of text, blocks and numeric data (including formulas and links to external spreadsheets such as Excel), be creatable from the TABLE command by row and column counts, and be adjustable through grips with table and cell styles.
notes: Added from help page "About Tables"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a 3x4 table with TABLE, drag a column grip to widen it and assert the width changes; link a cell to an Excel range and assert the values appear.

statement: Table styles must store cell styles for label and data cells that govern general (fill, alignment, format, margins), text and border properties, be managed with TABLESTYLE, be stored in drawings and templates, and be importable from other drawings.
notes: Added from help page "About Working With Table and Cell Styles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a table style with a red-filled title cell style, make a table with it and assert the title cell is red; import the style into another drawing and assert it exists.

statement: Table cells must hold text and one or more blocks, grow row height with content, support Tab and arrow navigation, in-place editing, block auto-fit to cell size, and a Manage Cell Content dialog for multiple blocks.

source.ref: Adding text and blocks to tables

notes: Added from help page "About Adding Text and Blocks to Tables"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Type two lines in a cell and assert row height grows; insert a block with auto-fit and assert it scales to the cell; add a second block and assert Manage Cell Content lists both.
